parsed.methodology: Our analysis synthesized qualitative insights from student and employer personas with quantitative data on retention, ATS friction, and CLR adoption to identify strategic opportunities for Northeastern University's co-op program.
parsed.storyArc: The current co-op system faces critical challenges in first-year retention and employer integration, necessitating a strategic shift towards a CLR-powered ecosystem, which can be achieved through a set of coordinated actions.

slides.title: Northeastern University must implement a CLR-powered co-op strategy to significantly improve first-year retention and streamline employer integration.
slides.rationale: This slide introduces the core recommendation and frames the entire presentation's objective.

slides.title: Current co-op challenges are eroding first-year retention and creating significant friction for key employers.
slides.rationale: This section header introduces the diagnosis phase of Rumelt's Kernel, setting up the problem statement.

slides.title: Nearly a quarter of first-year students transfer, with co-op uncertainty being a primary driver of mobility risk.
slides.rationale: This slide presents evidence of the first-year retention challenge, directly addressing a key research goal.

slides.title: Top employers face significant ATS friction due to NU's inability to export structured candidate data, hindering co-op placements.
slides.rationale: This slide provides evidence of the employer ATS friction, highlighting a critical barrier to effective co-op matching.

slides.title: The current co-op system creates a critical disconnect between student expectations, employer needs, and NU's data capabilities.
slides.rationale: This slide visually synthesizes the interconnected problems, demonstrating the systemic nature of the challenges identified.

slides.title: Northeastern University will adopt a Comprehensive Learner Record (CLR) as the foundation for a modernized co-op ecosystem.
slides.rationale: This section header introduces the guiding policy, clearly stating the strategic choice to address the diagnosed problems.

slides.title: A CLR-centric co-op strategy offers a singular path to address student uncertainty, employer friction, and NU's data limitations.
slides.rationale: This slide explicitly positions the CLR as the strategic solution that excludes alternatives, fulfilling the guiding policy requirement.

slides.title: Implementing a CLR-driven co-op strategy requires a coordinated set of actions across student experience, technology, and industry partnerships.
slides.rationale: This section header introduces the coherent actions phase, outlining the necessary steps to execute the guiding policy.

slides.title: Five strategic initiatives will integrate CLR across the co-op lifecycle to deliver immediate and long-term impact.
slides.rationale: This slide details the 5-7 coherent actions, ensuring they are MECE and directly support the CLR-centric guiding policy.

slides.title: These actions will significantly improve first-year retention, increase employer satisfaction, and position NU as a leader in experiential learning.
slides.rationale: This slide summarizes the expected positive outcomes and strategic benefits of implementing the proposed actions.

slides.title: Northeastern University is uniquely positioned to redefine the future of co-op through a strategic investment in CLR technology and student support.
slides.rationale: This concluding slide reiterates the main recommendation and emphasizes Northeastern's leadership opportunity.
